source.author: verg
source.text: Urbs antiqua fuit, Tyrii tenuere coloni, Karthago, Italiam contra Tiberinaque longe ostia, dives opum studiisque asperrima belli; quam Iuno fertur terris magis omnibus unam posthabita coluisse Samo; hic illius arma, hic currus fuit; hoc regnum dea gentibus esse, si qua fata sinant, iam tum tenditque fovetque.
source.text_original: Urbs antiqua fuit, Tyrii tenuere coloni, / Karthago, Italiam contra Tiberinaque longe / ostia, dives opum studiisque asperrima belli; / quam Iuno fertur terris magis omnibus unam / posthabita coluisse Samo; hic illius arma, / hic currus fuit; hoc regnum dea gentibus esse, / si qua fata sinant, iam tum tenditque fovetque.
source.text_english: There was an ancient city, held by Tyrian settlers, Carthage, opposite Italy and far from the mouths of the Tiber, rich in resources and most fierce in the pursuits of war. Juno is said to have cherished it more than all lands, preferring it even to Samos; here were her arms, here her chariot; even then the goddess was already striving and nurturing this that it should one day be the realm of the nations, if only the fates would allow.

reuse.text: hinc Danaum de fine sedet gentesque fovebo mox alias.
reuse.text_original: hinc Danaum de fine sedet gentesque fovebo / mox alias.
reuse.text_english: from here I sit at the end of the Danaans, and soon I shall cherish other nations as well
